subject: Preserve logs for Starlite production incident — retention exception request
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@starlite.io>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+incidents@starlite.io
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Production incident — request to preserve diagnostic data beyond standard window

Hi Sean,

We had a spike and a partial degradation on our Starlite production cluster that started at ~14:30 PT. Our SRE team needs several request traces and Redis KV snapshots from your runtime to complete root cause analysis. I understand Redwood’s standard ephemeral debug retention is short — however given the cross-system nature here, we need you to preserve the relevant request/response traces, KV snapshots, and chunked token logs for 7 days instead of the usual retention so our engineers can correlate with our traces.

Attached is a small CSV of trace IDs we believe are relevant and a short summary of the timeline.

Can Redwood hold this data and restrict access to the named engineers below until we confirm the RCA? We’re aiming to close the RCA within 5 business days, but would request a 7-day preservation window as a safety margin. Please advise what you need from us (signed waiver, POA) to approve.

Trace IDs (attached): starlite-trace-ids.csv
Primary contact: Maria Gomez (maria.gomez@starlite.io)
Severity: Sev2

Thanks,
Maria Gomez
Head of Infrastructure — Starlite
---
Attachment: starlite-trace-ids.csv (CSV, 12 rows)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@starlite.io>
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Production incident — request to preserve diagnostic data beyond standard window

Thanks Maria — looping in security (Priyom), CS ops (Marcus) and legal (Laura) to move this through the retention exception flow.

Summary: Starlite requests a 7-day preservation of: request/response traces, Redis KV snapshots, and token/chunk logs tied to the attached trace IDs. Access must be limited to 3 named engineers from Starlite and 2 Redwood engineers for debugging.

Immediate asks for internal:
- Priyom: can security approve a temporary extension for these trace IDs? If not 7 days, what minimum window do you recommend for effective debugging?
- Laura: what formal sign-off / waiver do you need from Starlite to proceed?
- Marcus: please confirm we can apply access restrictions and an audit trail for all accesses to these records.

I’ve attached the CSV Maria sent here for reference.

Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: starlite-trace-ids.csv (forwarded)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@starlite.io>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production incident — request to preserve diagnostic data beyond standard window

Thanks for the ping. A few clarifying questions before I greenlight:
1) Exact datasets: are we preserving request/response payloads that may contain customer PII (user-provided prompts) or only metadata/headers and tokenized logs?
2) Who needs access (list names/emails) and the specific justification for each person?
3) Is there any existing legal hold or other retention that would conflict?
4) Can Starlite sign a limited-scope waiver acknowledging the extra retention and agreeing to review the artifacts within the window?

Assuming minimal PII and that access is limited to named engineers, security is generally comfortable with a short exception. My suggestion is 72–96 hours for initial preservation; 7 days is longer than our normal exception practice but may be acceptable with documented approval and encryption-at-rest assurances.

I’ll open SEC ticket SEC-719 and add audit requirements. Please provide the list of Starlite engineers who will access.

- Priyom
Director, Security & Compliance
---
Related: Jira SEC-719 (created)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@starlite.io>
Date: Fri, 19 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production incident — request to preserve diagnostic data beyond standard window

I reviewed the ask. Legal can approve a limited, time-boxed retention exception provided we get:
- A signed retention-waiver (I’m attaching our template).
- A precise list of artifacts and the limited access roster (names + emails).
- A firm deletion schedule and verification that deletion will be auditable (screenshot/log).

I am comfortable approving a 96-hour retention window starting from the timestamp on Maria’s initial request, provided Priyom signs off on access controls. If Starlite requires 7 days, we’ll need an escalation to VP Legal for approval.

I’ve attached the retention-waiver-template.docx — please have Starlite sign and return.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: retention-waiver-template.docx

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@starlite.io>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Sep 2025 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Final — retention exception approved (96 hours) and next steps

All — quick summary and action items. Per the approvals above:
- Retention exception window: 96 hours starting 2025-09-18T15:04:00-07:00 (expires 2025-09-22T15:04:00-07:00).
- Scope: request/response traces, Redis KV snapshots, and tokenized chunk logs for trace IDs in starlite-trace-ids.csv.
- Access: Maria Gomez (maria.gomez@starlite.io), Carlos Herrera (carlos.herrera@starlite.io) from Starlite; Redwood engineers: Priyom Das (priyom.das@redwood.com), Anil Rao (anil.rao@redwood.com) — access will be granted with MFA and logged.
- Legal: Laura Bennett has the signed waiver on file (pending signature) — Starlite to return signed copy by EOD Monday.
- Security: Priyom will ensure encryption-at-rest and audit logging; SEC-719 will track access events.
- Deletion: On expiry, ops will run the deletion job and post screenshots of logs to SEC-719 and the Drive folder linked below.

Maria — please confirm you have the access list and that Starlite will sign the waiver. Marcus — please implement the access restrictions and attach audit screenshots to SEC-719 when deletion completes.

Thanks everyone — will follow up when deletion is complete.

Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
